cases.title: Anticipatory bail: State v. Ravi Kumar
cases.court: Court of the Additional Sessions Judge, Lucknow
cases.stage: Hearing on an application for anticipatory bail under Section 482, BNSS
cases.you_are: Counsel for the applicant, Ravi Kumar
facts: Ravi Kumar, 34, runs a small mobile repair shop in Aminabad.
A supplier, Sunil Traders, alleges Ravi took ₹2.4 lakh of phone parts on credit in March and never paid, and has filed an FIR for cheating under Section 318(4), BNS.
Ravi says he paid ₹1.6 lakh by UPI and that the remainder is a civil dispute over defective stock.
Ravi has no previous cases, has deep roots in Lucknow, and has offered to join the investigation.
The police have issued no notice under Section 35, BNSS so far; Ravi fears arrest.
bench_focus: Is this a civil dispute dressed as a criminal case?
Flight risk and roots in the community
Will the applicant cooperate with the investigation?

cases.title: Cheque dishonour: Meenakshi Sundaram v. Karthik Raja
cases.court: Court of the Judicial Magistrate, Saidapet, Chennai
cases.stage: Hearing on the complaint under Section 138, Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881
cases.you_are: Counsel for the complainant, Meenakshi Sundaram
facts: Meenakshi Sundaram lent ₹3,00,000 to her neighbour Karthik Raja in January for his daughter's college fees, by bank transfer.
Karthik gave a cheque for ₹3,00,000 dated 10 June. It was returned on 14 June with the memo 'Funds Insufficient'.
Meenakshi sent a demand notice by speed post on 2 July, received on 5 July.
No payment was made within 15 days. The complaint was filed on 8 August.
Karthik's defence: the cheque was a blank security cheque and the loan was ₹1,50,000, not ₹3,00,000.
bench_focus: Notice within 30 days of the return memo
Legally enforceable debt and the bank transfer

cases.title: Consumer complaint: Arjun Mehta v. ZipKart Electronics
cases.court: District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission, Pune
cases.stage: Final arguments on a consumer complaint
cases.you_are: The complainant, appearing in person (Section 70, Consumer Protection Act, 2019)
facts: Arjun Mehta bought a ₹42,000 laptop from ZipKart Electronics' website in February.
The screen started flickering within three weeks. The service centre kept it twice for 18 days in total.
ZipKart refused a refund, saying the 7-day return window was over and only repair is covered.
Arjun has the invoice, three service job sheets and emails showing six complaints.
He seeks a refund, ₹25,000 compensation for harassment and ₹5,000 costs.
bench_focus: Deficiency in service vs manufacturing defect
Does the return window bar a refund for a defect?
